- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > 3 days of negative values), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% in those periods.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often underestimates the continuation; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 10–15 day horizons; if recent 10-day average is > 10% above 30-day average, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to lag 1–2 days behind true trend; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is positive and price is flat or slightly down, model often forecasts downward; reverse direction if sentiment > 0.10 for 3+ days.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; if sentiment changes > 0.30 in one day, wait 2–3 days before adjusting forecast unless price is clearly trending.
